extracted.intended_audience: readers and researchers of 18th-century history and secret societies (general/historical audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive account of the organisational plan, methods, membership classes, and operations proposed by the German Union (a secret society) to promote 'enlightenment' and influence public opinion and the book trade in late-18th-century Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlistment through subscription and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective members must pay a rix-dahler and subscribe their acquiescence to the plan in order to be enrolled and receive subsequent documents (No. II oath, No. III Second Plan, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The address is an enlisting advertisement: 'after a few insignificant remarks on the Association, a rix-dahler is required along with the subscription of acquiescence in the plan' and payment triggers sending of the oath and plan materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath of secrecy for admitted members
rubrics_metrics.description: Admitted persons must sign an oath abjuring all treachery or discovery of the Association until circumstances make it proper to reveal themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No. II is a form of the Oath of secrecy; 'When any person writes to us, we send him an oath, by which he must abjure all treachery or discovery of the Association, till circumstances shall make it proper for us to come forward...'

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-tier membership structure (Ordinary vs Managing Brethren)
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership is divided into Ordinary Brethren (who know only the local literary society aspect) and Managing Brethren (who alone know the true aim and means of the Union).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The managing class 'alone know the aim of the association, and all the means for attaining it; and they alone constitute the UNION' while Ordinary Brethren are led to believe merely in a local literary society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Reading Societies as a front and recruiting ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish reading societies in every quarter to gather readers and identify promising, serious-minded individuals for secret recruitment into the Union's higher work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading Societies 'are to be formed in every quarter, and to be furnished with proper books.' Active Brethren observe in secret and 'select those whom they think valuable acquisitions' to invite into the inner work; attention must be paid to public taste but also to gradually direct reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional organisation into Provinces/Dioceses with Diocesans
rubrics_metrics.description: Once sufficient presence exists, divide fraternised parts of the nation into ten or twelve Provinces/Dioceses, each directed by a Diocesan who reports into a central Union-House.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan states: 'we now divide the fraternised part of the nation into ten or twelve Provinces or Dioceses, each directed by its Diocesan at his office; and these are so arranged in due subordination, that all business comes into the UNION-HOUSE as into the center of the whole.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Central secretary and Union-house to manage correspondence and commissioning
rubrics_metrics.description: A central secretary and Union-house are established to expedite business, receive reports, commission books, and coordinate the Union's operations nationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is 'a secretary and proper office in the center of the Association, where every thing is expedited, and all reports received.' The secretary commissions books conforming to the Association's aims and undertakes to commission for the curious in his neighbourhood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture and control of the bookselling trade
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically draw booksellers and the publishing trade into the Union so that authors publish through Union channels and the Union can increase distribution of approved works and diminish that of opposed writings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit: 'The Union considers it as a chief part of its secret plan of operation, to include the trade of bookselling in their circle.' The plan explains that by bringing trade into their hands, 'the writers who labour in the cause of superstition and restraint, will have neither a publisher nor readers.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a general literary Gazette/Review to unify and influence public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a Gazette or Review that unites members' talents, supplies political and literary intelligence in a form meant to 'strip' events to how they affect a rational man, and eventually supplant other gazettes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals: 'To introduce a general literary Gazette or Review... which, by uniting all the learned Brethren... may in time supplant every other Gazette.' It will include political news 'represented as it affects, or ought to affect, ourselves' and be published weekly at a low price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and gradual direction of public taste via chosen books
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and distribute books to reading societies that both comply with public taste and are skillfully directed to subjects that enlarge comprehension and habituate readers to novel ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan: 'attention must be paid to two things. The taste of the public must be complied with... But the general taste may, and must also be carefully and skilfully directed to subjects that will enlarge the comprehension... and by habituating the mind to novelty... will hinder the timid from being startled at doctrines and maxims which are singular.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret intelligence network (rapid, unsusceptible correspondence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a secret, rapid, hard-to-detect correspondence system to learn everything that goes on in the world for or against the cause and to coordinate secret operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as 'a secret correspondence that is quick, unsusceptible of all discovery or treachery, and attended with no expence, by which the business of the secret plan... is carried on.' There are hints of seeking influence over post-offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Lodges after a synod to transmit the 'plan of secret operation'
rubrics_metrics.description: After achieving numbers and holding a general synod, send a person with full powers to visit quarters, establish Lodges with ancient ritual, and verbally communicate the plan of secret operation and instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan: 'When this takes place, a general synod will be held... A proper person will set off from this synod, with full powers to visit every quarter... establish a Lodge after the ancient simple ritual, and will communicate verbally the plan of secret operation, and certain instructions.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Each Lodge establishes a managing fund and local agents (Expediteur)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Lodge must set up a managing fund/box and appoint a collector/agent to handle funds and to act as an Expediteur for the Union's local commercial and correspondence operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan requires 'a managing fund or box. Each Lodge will also establish a Reading Society... There must also be a collector and agent, (Expediteur), so that in a moment the Union will have its offices or comptoirs in every quarter.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership classes with defined duties, privileges, and remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide literary members into classes—Mesopolites (Metropolitans), Aldermen, Men, Cadets—each with assigned occupations, degrees of masonry affiliation, and economic arrangements for publication returns and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'An Alderman receives for an original work 80 per cent. of the returns, and 70 for a translation. The member of the next class receives 60, and the Cadet 50. As to the expence of printing, the Alderman pays nothing... but the Man and the Cadet must pay one-half.' Roles: Mesopolites attached to archive-office; Aldermen selected as Diocesans and Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imprimatur and internal recommendation published externally
rubrics_metrics.description: Works approved by an Alderman or formally approved will receive an imprimatur published in the General Review/Gazette, which serves as a powerful recommendation and aids distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: 'A dissertation by a Man, or by a Cadet, provided that the manuscript is documented by an Alderman, or formally approved by him... This imprimatur... is to be published in the General Review or Gazette.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial strategy: subscription model to fund publications and central office
rubrics_metrics.description: Fund key publications and the secretary's office by subscription calls to members and early advances of money to purchase paper and support printing for fairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No. V asks members to 'encourage the work by subscribing, and by exerting more than their usual activity in procuring subscriptions... Four persons are named as Diocesans, who are to receive the money, which they beg may be speedily advanced in order to purchase paper.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactical suppression and marginalisation of opposing writings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce the influence of 'fanatical' or opposed writers by using Union control of publishers and reviewers to banish or warn against such writings, thereby depriving them of publishers and readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit strategy: 'we shall bring it about, that at last the writers who labour in the cause of superstition and restraint, will have neither a publisher nor readers.' Also the Union may 'banish into the shade all the fanatical writings which appear in the reviews that are commonly read, or to warn the public against them.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic placement of members to influence appointments and offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Place Brethren into positions (courts, families, public offices, teachers, tutors) so the Union can influence appointments of court-officers, stewards, secretaries, parish-priests, public teachers, and private tutors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ultimate aims include: 'by our means will be put in a condition that enables them to work in silence upon all courts, families, and individuals in every quarter, and acquire an influence in the appointment of court-officers, stewards, secretaries, parish-priests, public teachers, and private tutors.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-facing declaration strategy and use of an exterior literary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Control the Union's public image by presenting an exterior literary work (e.g., 'On Instruction') as the Association's avowed piece, append lists of respectable members optionally, and thereby justify an outward, respectable presence while retaining secret aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H. Barthels suggests annexing a sheet as an appendix to 'On Instruction' declaring it the work of the Society as 'a sufficient indication of its most honourable aim' and requests members who wish to share honour to send names for that Appendix; this is intended to inform the public only of the exterior of the Society.
